errors.english:
There is truly no other meditative concentration,
Because any other is a lack of equipoise.
errors.why: The verse says that the intellect engaging an object on which the mind is fixed is not truly samādhi, because it is not real equipoise; the English instead affirms object-focused equipoise as the only samādhi and applies the reason to 'any other'.

errors.english: the characteristics of those who designate
errors.why: The Tibetan means the defining marks by which [these factors] are designated are not separately distinct, not the characteristics of persons who designate.

errors.english: The perfect one line of text follows, cut off at the page break
errors.why: The side ends with the single word rdzogs pa'i; the rest is unmarked translator meta-text.

fix.find: The perfect one line of text follows, cut off at the page break

note: Accurate verse translation of the samādhi passage on the whole, with one misconstrued verse on object-focused equipoise and unbracketed glosses after Sanskrit terms.

errors.english: stealing from houses where food is prepared
errors.why: Ro here is 'corpse': the house where corpses are deposited (a charnel house), which is why northerners call it 'grave robbing'.

fix.find: stealing from houses where food is prepared
fix.replace: stealing from houses where corpses are deposited

errors.english: One who is not overcome by the disease of madness is "one who has become insane."
errors.why: The Tibetan says one is 'insane' because one is overcome by the disease of madness; the negation is added.

fix.find: One who is not overcome by the disease of madness
fix.replace: One who is overcome by the disease of madness

errors.english: One whose thoughts are constantly interrupted and scattered is "one with a distracted mind."
errors.why: Rgyun mi 'chad par means 'uninterruptedly': the deranged-mind case is the continuous one, in contrast to the intermittent madman just described.

errors.english: A "miscarriage" [note: literally: "ruined womb"] refers to the means by which a womb becomes empty.
errors.why: Mngal rlugs pa (garbhapātana) is a procured abortion, defined as a 'means' to empty the womb, not a spontaneous miscarriage.

note: A usable rendering of the Vinaya glossary, but it adds a negation in the definition of madness and mistakes the charnel-house theft.

errors.english: In response to that, it is said: The houses, parks, and so forth that are perceived there do not arise dependently [note: in the sense of being real entities].
errors.why: The reply is a reductio: if the perceived houses were not dependently arisen, grass and wood would not be either, so the houses are dependently arisen (as the next side concludes); the English states the opponent's premise as the author's thesis and the note reinforces it.

fix.find: In response to that, it is said: The houses, parks, and so forth that are perceived there do not arise dependently [note: in the sense of being real entities]. Just like those houses and parks, the grass and wood [the argument continues]...
fix.replace: In response to that, it is said: If the houses, parks, and so forth that are perceived there did not arise dependently, then, just like those houses and parks, the grass and wood [would not arise dependently either]...

note: The gandharva-city, magic-show and mirage examples are rendered faithfully, but the author's reply to the objection is inverted at the end of the side.
A faithful and technically sound rendering of the commentary on the two components of the ālambana; only minor stray markup (a column-break tag) remains.

errors.english: they are explained separately here
errors.why: The Tibetan says they are NOT explained separately here, since offerings were treated earlier and rejoicing comes later.

fix.replace: they are not explained separately here

errors.english: should it not be explained again here?
errors.why: The objection asserts that refuge should not be explained here because it was already explained above; the English question implies the opposite.

fix.find: should it not be explained again here?
fix.replace: it should not be explained here again."

note: The vocabulary of the two kinds of misdeed and the four powers is good, but two negations flip the argument about why some powers are not treated here.

errors.english: the positions of those who rely [note: on external objects] and those who do not
errors.why: The contrast, with the edition note and the following lines, is between the positions that things are stable (brtan pa) and that they are not stable (momentary), not reliance on external objects.

fix.find: the positions of those who rely [note: on external objects] and those who do not
fix.replace: the positions that things are stable and that they are not stable

errors.english: the opponent's position is challenged on both sides
errors.why: The opponent raises an objection against both alternatives (with and without aspect), to which the author then replies that the objection applies equally to both parties.

fix.find: the opponent's position is challenged on both sides
fix.replace: the opponent raises an objection against both alternatives

errors.english: Even if I claim that
errors.why: No first-person claim is in the Tibetan; the clause states the consequence by which 'you' must accept such a cognition.

errors.english: could not be established at the end of the line
errors.why: 'At the end of the line' is stray meta-text, not in the Tibetan.

fix.find: could not be established at the end of the line

note: The overall dialectic on cognition with and without aspect is followed, but the stable/momentary contrast is mistranslated and the roles of objector and respondent are swapped.

errors.english: The neutral and the unattractive are also each divided into three
errors.why: To get the stated total of seven, the neutral remain one class and only the disliked are divided into three; 'each' produces nine, and the translator's note tries to explain away the mismatch.

errors.english: Initially, one should meditate intensely on those who are moderately dear, such as parents and so on.
errors.why: The moderately dear are to be cultivated as being like one's parents (the most dear), as the parallel final step shows; parents are not examples of the moderately dear.

note: A sound translation of the three kinds of love and the graded meditation, with the sevenfold division and the first step slightly misconstrued.

errors.english: Most people are not attached to the common
errors.why: Dharmakīrti says most people ARE attached to the vulgar (prākṛta), as the commentary's own gloss of the verse confirms.

fix.find: Most people are not attached to the common
fix.replace: Most people are attached to the common

errors.english: If others besides myself see this text and subsequently act for the benefit of others, it will become meaningful.
errors.why: It is the text that accomplishes others' benefit when others besides the author see it, not the readers acting for others.

errors.english: The water of the eight-limbed river flows along
errors.why: The eight qualities (yan lag brgyad) belong to the water, which flows in rivers, not to the river.

note: Generally accurate on Bodhicaryāvatāra 1.2–3 and its quotations, but a dropped-in negation inverts Dharmakīrti's verse.

errors.english: "If it depends only on what appears in that way,"
errors.why: Yin la rag is a concessive idiom ('granted that it does appear thus'): the opponent concedes that the inner object appears in consciousness and then asks how a co-arisen part can be its condition; 'depends' makes the next sentence circular nonsense.

fix.find: "If it depends only on what appears in that way," and so forth. This means that the appearance of the object of knowledge the thing to be known which exists within consciousness depends upon that very appearance.
fix.replace: "Granted that it does appear in that way," and so forth. This means: granted that the internally existing object of knowledge does appear in consciousness.

errors.english: because they are mistaken
errors.why: 'Khrul ba here is the logical sense 'deviating', that is, not invariably concomitant (vyabhicāra), not 'mistaken'.

note: The reply on the ālambana-pratyaya and the four conditions is well handled, but the opponent's concessive opening is garbled.

errors.english: perceive "this is not similar"
errors.why: The verse asks how, if there is no similarity, one understands 'this is similar'; the negation is added.

errors.english: There is no need for the functioning of every valid cognition in that regard. If you ask why this occurs through the assembly of causes and conditions without relying on investigation and analysis, we reply:
errors.why: The whole passage is the opponent's rejoinder (ending in zhe na): the operation of all pramāṇas simply occurs, since the causal complex arises that way by force of its causes and is not open to the challenge 'why does this happen thus?'; the English splits it and has the opponent ask the question.

note: The upamāna-as-inference argument is mostly clear, but a negation is added in the verse on similarity and the opening exchange is mis-segmented.
